sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Strategic Objective**: To demonstrate that the Indian people were not supporting the war effort voluntarily and to assert the **Right to Free Speech** against the war.
• **Gandhian Philosophy**: It was a **moral protest** rather than a mass movement, ensuring that the British war effort was not disrupted while maintaining the Congress's anti-war stance.
• **Operational Mechanism**: Satyagrahis were carefully selected by Gandhi; they had to inform the District Magistrate of their intent to speak against the war at a specific time and place, leading to their inevitable arrest.
• **Key Metric**: Over 25,000 Satyagrahis were imprisoned by May 1941, showcasing the movement's disciplined, non-violent nature.

The immediate trigger; the Congress rejected the offer as it failed to provide a clear timeline for Dominion Status, leading to the launch of the Satyagraha.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Symbolic Protest**: The movement focused on the individual's right to express anti-war views, keeping the spirit of resistance alive without triggering mass repression.
• **Political Continuity**: It kept the Congress organization intact and active during the war years when mass mobilization was deemed risky.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Limited impact on the British war policy; lack of mass participation meant the government could easily contain it.
• **Solutions**: Transitioned into the 'Quit India' movement once the failure of the Cripps Mission made mass struggle inevitable.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: V-J-B (Vinoba, Jawaharlal, Brahma).
• **Decoded Meaning**: The sequence of the first three Satyagrahis: Vinoba Bhave, Jawaharlal Nehru, and Brahma Datt.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often frames questions suggesting Individual Satyagraha was a mass movement. It was strictly an 'Individual' movement to avoid mass repression and maintain non-violent discipline.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Moral Protest' and 'Symbolic Resistance' to describe the movement's strategic intent in the context of the Second World War.

keyTakeaways: Individual Satyagraha was a strategic, non-mass movement launched in 1940.
The primary goal was to assert the right to free speech against the war effort.
Vinoba Bhave was the first, and Jawaharlal Nehru was the second Satyagrahi.
